description: This topic explains the four types of conditional (if) sentences in English, their tense structures, related words such as unless and provided that, basic mixed conditionals, punctuation and common errors.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence is a zero conditional expressing a general truth?

options.text: If you heat ice, it melts.
If you heated ice, it would melt.
If you had heated ice, it would have melted.
If you will heat ice, it melts.

mcq.explanation: The zero conditional uses the present simple in both clauses to state facts and general truths.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct first conditional sentence about a real future possibility.

options.text: If it rains tomorrow, we will stay at home.
If it will rain tomorrow, we stay at home.
If it rained tomorrow, we will stay at home.
If it rains tomorrow, we stayed at home.

mcq.explanation: The first conditional uses present simple in the if-clause and 'will + base verb' in the main clause.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence is a correct second conditional?

options.text: If I won the lottery, I would build a school.
If I win the lottery, I would build a school.
If I won the lottery, I will build a school.
If I would win the lottery, I built a school.

mcq.explanation: The second conditional uses past simple in the if-clause and 'would + base verb' in the main clause to express an unreal or hypothetical present situation.

mcq.questionText: Identify the correct third conditional sentence.

options.text: If she had studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
If she studied harder, she would have passed the exam.
If she had studied harder, she would pass the exam.
If she has studied harder, she would have passed the exam.

mcq.explanation: The third conditional uses past perfect in the if-clause and 'would have + past participle' in the main clause to talk about an unreal past.

mcq.questionText: What does 'unless' mean in the sentence: 'You will fail unless you work hard.'?

options.text: if you do not
if you do
because you do
although you do

mcq.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not'; the sentence means 'You will fail if you do not work hard.'

options.text: If you arrive early, we will start the meeting.
If you arrive early we will start the meeting.
We will start the meeting, if you arrive early.
If you arrive early; we will start the meeting.

mcq.explanation: When the if-clause comes first, it is followed by a comma. When the main clause comes first, no comma is needed.

mcq.questionText: Complete: 'If water reaches 100 degrees Celsius, it _____ .'

options.text: boils
will boil
would boil
boiled

mcq.explanation: This is a scientific fact, so the zero conditional is used with present simple in both clauses.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct conditional: 'If I were you, I _____ apologise to the teacher.'

options.text: would
will
had
have

mcq.explanation: This is a second conditional giving advice; 'were' is used with all subjects and the main clause takes 'would + base verb'.

mcq.questionText: Which phrase correctly completes a condition meaning 'on condition that'? 'You may go out _____ you finish your homework first.'

options.text: provided that
unless
in case not
although

mcq.explanation: 'Provided that' and 'as long as' express a condition that must be met, meaning 'only if'.

mcq.questionText: In which sentence should 'when' be used instead of 'if'?

options.text: _____ the sun rises, it becomes light. (a regular, certain event)
_____ it rains tomorrow, we might cancel. (uncertain)
_____ you study hard, you may pass. (uncertain)
When the sun rises, it becomes light.

mcq.explanation: 'When' is used for events that are certain to happen, while 'if' is used for uncertain or possible events.

options.text: If I will see her, I will tell her.
If I see her, I will tell her.
If I saw her, I would tell her.
If I had seen her, I would have told her.

mcq.explanation: We do not use 'will' in the if-clause of a first conditional; it should be 'If I see her, I will tell her.'

mcq.questionText: Identify the basic mixed conditional sentence.

options.text: If I had taken the medicine, I would feel better now.
If I take the medicine, I will feel better.
If I took the medicine, I would feel better.
If I had taken the medicine, I would have felt better.

mcq.explanation: A mixed conditional links a past condition (past perfect) to a present result ('would + base verb', shown by 'now').

mcq.questionText: Complete the second conditional: 'If they _____ more time, they would finish the project.'

options.text: had
have
will have
would have

mcq.explanation: The second conditional uses the past simple in the if-clause, so 'had' is correct.

mcq.questionText: Which sentence uses 'as long as' correctly to express a condition?

options.text: You can borrow my pen as long as you return it.
You can borrow my pen as long as not you return it.
As long as you returned it, you borrow my pen.
You can borrow my pen as long as you will return it.

mcq.explanation: 'As long as' means 'only if' and is followed by the present simple when talking about the future.

mcq.questionText: What kind of conditional expresses regret about the past?

options.text: third conditional
zero conditional
first conditional
second conditional

mcq.explanation: The third conditional talks about an unreal past and is often used to express regret about something that did not happen.

fib.questionText: Zero conditional: 'If you mix blue and yellow, you _____ green.' (get)
fib.explanation: The zero conditional uses present simple in both clauses for general truths.

fib.questionText: First conditional: 'If we leave now, we _____ catch the bus.' (use will)
fib.explanation: The main clause of a first conditional uses 'will + base verb' for a real future result.

fib.questionText: Second conditional: 'If I _____ rich, I would help the poor.' (be)
fib.explanation: In second conditionals 'were' is used for all subjects after 'if' to show an unreal situation.

fib.questionText: Third conditional: 'If they had left earlier, they _____ have arrived on time.' (use would)
fib.explanation: The third conditional main clause uses 'would have + past participle'.

fib.questionText: Rewrite using 'unless': 'You will be late if you do not hurry.' = 'You will be late _____ you hurry.'
fib.explanation: 'Unless' means 'if not', so it replaces 'if you do not'.

fib.questionText: Punctuation: 'If the weather is good_____ we will play football.' Fill the blank with the correct punctuation mark.
fib.explanation: When the if-clause comes first, it is separated from the main clause by a comma.

fib.questionText: Condition word: 'I will lend you the book _____ that you give it back tomorrow.' (means 'on condition')
fib.explanation: 'Provided that' introduces a necessary condition, meaning 'only if'.

fib.questionText: Choose 'when' or 'if': '_____ the bell rings, the lesson ends. (a regular, certain event)'
fib.explanation: 'When' is used for certain, regular events; 'if' is used for uncertain ones.

fib.questionText: Second conditional: 'If she knew the answer, she _____ tell us.' (use would)
fib.explanation: The second conditional uses past simple in the if-clause and 'would + base verb' in the main clause.

fib.questionText: Third conditional: 'If I _____ known you were sick, I would have visited you.' (use the past perfect of 'know')
fib.explanation: The if-clause of a third conditional uses the past perfect: 'had known'.

tf.questionText: The zero conditional uses the present simple tense in both the if-clause and the main clause.
tf.explanation: The zero conditional describes general truths using present simple in both clauses.

tf.questionText: In the first conditional, we use 'will' in the if-clause.
tf.explanation: We use present simple in the if-clause and 'will' only in the main clause of a first conditional.

tf.questionText: The second conditional talks about an unreal or imaginary present or future situation.
tf.explanation: The second conditional describes situations that are unlikely or imaginary in the present or future.

tf.questionText: The third conditional uses 'would have + past participle' in the main clause.
tf.explanation: The third conditional main clause uses 'would have + past participle' to discuss an unreal past.
'Unless' means 'if not', which is the opposite of 'if'.

tf.questionText: When the if-clause comes after the main clause, a comma is normally not needed.
tf.explanation: A comma is used only when the if-clause comes first; it is omitted when the main clause comes first.

tf.questionText: 'Provided that' and 'as long as' can both be used to introduce a condition.
tf.explanation: Both phrases mean 'only if' and introduce a condition that must be met.

tf.questionText: We use 'when' instead of 'if' when we are sure something will happen.
tf.explanation: 'When' is used for certain events, while 'if' is used for uncertain or possible ones.

tf.questionText: In the sentence 'If I had money, I would buy a car', the speaker has plenty of money now.
tf.explanation: This is a second conditional showing an unreal present; it means the speaker does not have the money now.

tf.questionText: A mixed conditional can connect a past condition to a present result.
tf.explanation: A basic mixed conditional links a past unreal condition (past perfect) to a present result (would + base verb).

summary.questionText: State the tense structure of the zero conditional.
summary.explanation: The zero conditional uses present simple in both clauses for facts and general truths.

summary.questionText: State the tense structure of the first conditional.
summary.correctAnswer: If + present simple, will + base verb.
summary.explanation: The first conditional expresses a real future possibility.

summary.questionText: State the tense structure of the second conditional.
summary.correctAnswer: If + past simple, would + base verb.
summary.explanation: The second conditional expresses an unreal or hypothetical present or future situation.

summary.questionText: State the tense structure of the third conditional.
summary.correctAnswer: If + past perfect, would have + past participle.
summary.explanation: The third conditional expresses an unreal past, often showing regret.

summary.questionText: Explain the meaning of 'unless' in one short sentence.
summary.explanation: 'Unless' introduces a negative condition equivalent to 'if not'.

summary.questionText: Explain the punctuation rule for conditional sentences.
summary.correctAnswer: Use a comma after the if-clause when it comes first; no comma when the main clause comes first.
summary.explanation: Comma placement depends on the order of the clauses.

summary.questionText: Give two phrases that can replace 'if' to express a condition.
summary.explanation: Both phrases mean 'only if' and introduce a condition.

summary.questionText: When should you use 'when' rather than 'if' in a conditional-like sentence?
summary.correctAnswer: Use 'when' for events that are certain to happen and 'if' for uncertain ones.

summary.questionText: Briefly describe what a basic mixed conditional does.
summary.correctAnswer: It links a past unreal condition to a present result.
summary.explanation: A mixed conditional combines a past perfect if-clause with a present 'would + base verb' result.

summary.questionText: Name one common error students make with the first conditional.
summary.correctAnswer: Using 'will' in the if-clause instead of the present simple.
summary.explanation: We say 'If it rains', not 'If it will rain'.

hoq.questionText: Transform into a third conditional: 'I did not save money, so I could not buy the phone.' Which is correct?

options.text: If I had saved money, I could have bought the phone.
If I saved money, I could buy the phone.
If I save money, I can buy the phone.
If I had saved money, I can buy the phone.

hoq.explanation: The original is an unreal past, so the third conditional uses past perfect plus 'could have + past participle'.

hoq.questionText: Combine into a mixed conditional: 'She did not learn to swim. She is afraid of the water now.' Which is correct?

options.text: If she had learned to swim, she would not be afraid of the water now.
If she learned to swim, she would not have been afraid of the water now.
If she had learned to swim, she would not have been afraid of the water now.
If she learns to swim, she will not be afraid of the water now.

hoq.explanation: A past condition ('had learned') links to a present result ('would not be ... now'), so a mixed conditional is required.

hoq.questionText: Rewrite using 'unless' without changing the meaning: 'The plants will die if we do not water them.' Which is correct?

options.text: The plants will die unless we water them.
The plants will die unless we do not water them.
Unless we water them, the plants will not die.
The plants will die unless we will water them.

hoq.explanation: 'Unless' already means 'if not', so we drop the negative and use the present simple: 'unless we water them'.
